issues.label: Hospital emergency wait times
issues.quote: Patients are waiting longer in our emergency departments than at any time in the past decade.

issues.label: Grant program probity
issues.quote: Grants were awarded to projects the department’s own assessors ranked lowest.

issues.label: Health records cyber incidents
issues.quote: Thousands of patient records were exposed, and the agency still cannot say how.

issues.label: Major project cost overruns
issues.quote: The project is now two years late and hundreds of millions over its original budget.

issues.label: Social housing maintenance backlogs
issues.quote: Tenants have waited more than a year for basic repairs to be done.

issues.label: Use of consultants and contractors
issues.quote: The department spent more on consultants last year than on its own frontline staff.

issues.label: Youth justice program outcomes
issues.quote: The government cannot tell this House whether the program has reduced reoffending.

issues.label: NDIS provider fraud controls
issues.quote: Fraudulent providers are draining money meant for participants.

issues.label: Audit office independence and funding
issues.quote: An Auditor-General who depends on the government for funding is not truly independent.

issues.label: School building program delays
issues.quote: Schools promised for this year still don’t have a builder.

issues.label: Council financial sustainability
issues.quote: Councils are running down their reserves just to keep basic services going.

issues.label: Disaster recovery funding
issues.quote: Communities hit by the floods are still waiting for recovery money promised a year ago.

issues.label: Closing the Gap reporting
issues.quote: We are told targets are on track, but the data to prove it has not been published.

issues.label: Water and energy project costs
issues.quote: The cost of this water project has doubled and no one in government will explain why.

issues.label: Public sector labour hire
issues.quote: Agencies are paying labour-hire rates for roles that have sat vacant for years.

issues.label: Out-of-home care placements
issues.quote: Children are being placed in motels because there is nowhere else for them to go.

items.rep: Administration of the Community Grants Hub
items.speaker: Hon. R. Carter
items.headline: Minister for Finance disputes ANAO report on Administration of the Community Grants Hub
items.summary: The Minister for Finance rejected key findings of the ANAO report on Administration of the Community Grants Hub, saying it relied on outdated data and overlooked recent changes.
items.why: A minister disputing findings on the floor usually leads to committee follow-up. Worth preparing a response line.
items.reason: Disputes the accuracy of the report’s data
items.quote: With respect, the Auditor-General has relied on figures that are simply out of date.

items.rep: Administration of the Community Grants Hub
items.speaker: Ms L. Nguyen
items.headline: Opposition cites ANAO report on Administration of the Community Grants Hub
items.summary: The opposition used the ANAO report on Administration of the Community Grants Hub to argue the program is failing, and called for its recommendations to be adopted in full.
items.why: The report is now part of the political debate. Expect more questions while Parliament sits.
items.reason: Relies on the report’s findings as evidence
items.quote: The Auditor-General’s report makes it plain: this program is not delivering for the people who need it.

items.speaker: Mr D. Walsh
items.reason: Factual description, no view on the office
items.headline: Estimates: ANAO budget flat in real terms
items.why: A flat budget may reduce the number of performance audits next year.
items.quote: The audit office’s appropriation is unchanged from last year, which is a cut in real terms.
items.summary: Budget estimates debate noted the ANAO appropriation is unchanged — a real-terms cut after inflation.

items.speaker: Hon. P. Singh
items.headline: Call for an audit of Defence consultant spend
items.summary: A crossbench member asked the Auditor-General to examine Defence consultant spend, citing rising costs and poor public reporting.
items.why: A public call for an audit. Check whether it fits the forward program.
items.quote: I call on the Auditor-General to examine Defence consultant spend as a matter of urgency.

items.speaker: Dr K. Moore
items.headline: Questions raised over NDIS provider fraud controls
items.summary: Members pressed the government on NDIS provider fraud controls, citing cost and timing figures not yet publicly reported.
items.why: Not covered by the current audit program, and raised more than once this period.
items.quote: Every month we wait, the bill to taxpayers gets bigger, and the minister still won’t give us the numbers.

items.speaker: Ms T. Brennan
items.headline: Government responds to recommendations on Defence major projects report
items.summary: The government accepted 6 of 8 recommendations from the ANAO report on Defence major projects report and gave timelines for the rest.
items.why: Sets the baseline for any follow-up audit of this report.
items.quote: The government has accepted six of the eight recommendations made by the Auditor-General.

items.headline: Annual Audit Work Program 2026–27: 2 topics added, 1 deferred
items.summary: The ANAO published an updated program. Added: Fraud control in the NDIS; Defence contractor management. One topic moved to next year.
items.why: Changes what the office will report on in the next 12 months.
